flagged.evidence: Step 2.1 says, “The sum of the constituents in one Galois orbit is stable under \(\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)\), hence descends to an \(F\)-subrepresentation of \(V\).” Its only cited fact, [L2], states only the base-change isomorphism \(E\otimes_F\operatorname{End}_G(V)\cong\operatorname{End}_G(E\otimes_FV)\). That does not state or prove Galois descent of a stable E-subrepresentation (or of its projector). The descent assertion is the essential step used to conclude that one orbit is all constituents.

[L1] claims “The Schur index divides the degree of an irreducible representation” and cites thm-character-of-an-irreducible-over-a-nonsplitting-field. That theorem states only \(\dim_FV=m[F(\chi):F]\chi(1)\), where \(m\) is the multiplicity in that scalar extension; it does not state \(m_{\mathbb Q}(\chi)\mid\chi(1)\). Nevertheless step 2.1 concludes “By [L1], the index divides \(\chi(1)=2\).” The nearby corollary cor-schur-index-divides-the-representation-degree likewise proves only \(m_K(\chi)\mid\dim_KV\), not the asserted divisibility of \(\chi(1)\). Thus the cited dependency does not license the restriction needed to conclude the index is two.

The fact is written “Since \(E\) splits \(G\), \(operatorname{End}_G(U)=E\).” The missing backslash means the displayed left side is not \(\operatorname{End}_G(U)\), so the asserted endomorphism-ring equality is not a well-formed mathematical expression.

The proof works in \(E\otimes_KD_V\) but says “Because \(z\otimes1\) is fixed by \(\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)\).” For \(z\in D_V\), \(z\otimes1\) is not an element of \(E\otimes_KD_V\); the typed element is \(1\otimes z\).
